newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha prices jump, nearby supply tight.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha prices jump, nearby supply tight.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices jumped on Friday, triggered by overnight gains in crude prices and keen end-user buying interest in prompt months, traders said.
Intermonth-spreads rose, reflecting unexpectedly tight supplies in nearby months, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha first-half April was assessed at about $238.50/240.00 up $4.00 from Thursday levels. Second-half March was assessed about $240.25/242.50.
The one-month spread from first-half April was assessed at $4.75/6.00, up sharply from Thursday's $3.50/4.00.
Traders said first-half March cargoes were scarce.
In early Thursday trade, second-half March/second-half April switched hands at $4.50, traders said. At least three Japanese buyers are looking for March cargoes, they said.

On Wednesday, a Japanese petrochemical firm bought a second-half March cargo at around $4.50 above the mean of Japanese quotes. The same firm earlier in the week bought a first-half March cargo at around the same price.
"Market sentiment is very strong, in spite of reports of output cuts at Japanese ethylene makers," a trader said.
